findings.reason: The shared cut at c000002 (131.64s) is flagged compiler_quantized_inside_detected_speech and detector_recognition_gap_disagreement, and the coverage intervals confirm it: the detector reports continuous speech 129314-136094ms, while the nearest transcribed words are w000275 'almost.' ending at 130909ms (section-0001's last sentence, s000025) and w000276 'There's' starting at 132349ms (section-0002's first sentence, s000026). The ~1.4s transcription gap around the cut may contain untranscribed speech that would be split across the two chapters; this remains unverified from text evidence alone and is reported as uncertainty, not a confirmed broken word. Editorially, the cut also separates the book exchange ('Congratulations on the upcoming book.' / 'It's ready almost.', s000024-s000025, kept in section-0001) from its direct follow-up 'There's a lot of energy in your books.' (s000026, opened by section-0002), so the surrounding book-topic context straddles the boundary.

The shared cut at c000004 (238.08s), which closes kept section-0003 and precedes the dropped fragment section-0004, falls inside a detector speech interval (236734-240040ms). The nearest transcribed words are w000511 'digression.' ending at 236596ms (end of complete sentence s000049, the kept section's last sentence) and w000512 'So' starting at 239577ms (first word of the dropped incomplete fragment s000050). The ~3s untranscribed gap between them is covered by detected speech, so the exact split point within it carries timing uncertainty; any untranscribed speech in that gap cannot be attributed to a side from text evidence alone. This is reported as uncertainty only, not a confirmed broken word. The drop of s000050 'So what is' itself is a justified, explicitly reasoned drop of an unfinished source-ending fragment and is not a kept-content defect.
